# Settings reference

> **Type:** reference · **Status:** released (generated from the code)

Every option of `maarse-host` and `maarse-server`. **The primary way to change them is the web client (Settings tab, or Settings page in the Android app).** Saving there writes `settings.txt` in the data folder and restarts the host. You can also edit `settings.txt` by hand: one option per line, exactly as listed below, for example:

```text
--public-addr server.example.org:4242
--region dk
--mail-quota-mb 500
```

Lines starting with `#` are comments. `settings.txt` is read first; options given on the command line (for example in a start script) win. `--data` and `--help` are not allowed in the file. Command-line use exists for the very first start and for scripts; it is not the recommended way to configure a running host.

Back to the [documentation index](../index.md) · How-to: [run a host or server](../guides/run-a-server.md)

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--data <folder>` | where identity and settings are stored (default: maarse-data) |
| `--http <addr:port>` | web client and WebSocket (default: 127.0.0.1:8080, 'off' disables) |
| `--listen <addr:port>` | accept backbone connections over TCP (default: 127.0.0.1:4242, 'off' disables) |
| `--peer <host:port>` | connect to another maarse-host (can be repeated) |
| `--serial <port>` | LoRa node in modem mode, e.g. COM3 or /dev/ttyACM0 |
| `--baud <rate>` | serial baud rate (default: 115200) |
| `--serial-link <port>[:baud]` | direct link to another maarse-host over a serial line (null-modem cable, USB-serial, transparent radio modem); default 115200 baud. At 230400 baud or more it counts as backbone (like TCP), below that as a slow radio link (can be repeated) |
| `--kiss <port>[:baud]` | KISS TNC on a serial port, e.g. a packet radio TNC or an RNode-like KISS device (default 9600 baud; can be repeated). Counts as a slow radio link |
| `--kiss-tcp <host:port>` | KISS TNC over TCP, e.g. Direwolf on port 8001 (reconnects every 5 s; can be repeated) |
| `--kiss-txdelay <N>` | KISS TXDELAY sent to the TNC, in 10 ms units |
| `--kiss-persist <N>` | KISS persistence (0-255) |
| `--kiss-slottime <N>` | KISS slot time, in 10 ms units |
| `--kiss-callsign <CALL[-SSID]>` | wrap KISS packets in AX.25 UI frames from this callsign (to QST), for amateur-radio identification |
| `--udp-listen <addr:port>` | UDP socket for backbone peers, e.g. 0.0.0.0:4243; senders become peers and are forgotten after 3 minutes of silence |
| `--udp-peer <host:port>` | send to this UDP peer (can be repeated) |
| `--udp-broadcast <port>` | find peers on the LAN: broadcast to this port and accept packets from any sender on it |
| `--public` | also connect to the public backbone servers (nj01.dk.eu.maarse.dk:4242; more are found from there) |
| `--max-file <KB>` | largest file sent and received (default: 1024) |
| `--history-days <N>` | keep message history for N days, so several screens see the whole conversation (default: 90). NOTE: stored unencrypted in <data>/history |
| `--no-history` | keep no message history on disk |
| `--mailbox <address>` | use this node as my mailbox while I am offline |
| `--file-mailbox-mb <MB>` | space for files to recipients who are offline (default: 200, 0 disables the file mailbox). Files expire after 7 days |
| `--file-mailbox-recipient-mb <MB>` | of which at most per recipient (default: 20) |
| `--public-addr <host:port>` | my public backbone address: makes me a DHT node, so others can look up the addresses I can reach |
| `--dht <host:port>` | DHT seed (lookups only, can be repeated). --peer and --public are also used as seeds |
| `--dht-allow-private <host:port>` | allow a private DHT-discovered endpoint without using it as a seed (can be repeated) |
| `--seed-dns <name[:port]>` | a DNS name with several backbone nodes behind it; all of them become peers (can be repeated) |
| `--set-admin-password <password>` | maarse-server: set the dashboard's admin password and exit |
| `--set-admin-password-stdin` | set the dashboard password from one line on stdin and exit |
| `--no-post-office` | do not keep mail for others (told to the backbone, so no one picks this host as a replica) |
| `--modem-key <passphrase>` | Wi-Fi LoRa modems must prove this key (set the same passphrase in the modem); maarse-server accepts no Wi-Fi modem without it (at least 12 characters) |
| `--modem-tcp <host:port> a LoRa modem as a plain byte stream over TCP (the` | serial modem protocol; the Android app bridges it to a radio over Bluetooth). Key in modem-tcp-key.txt. |
| `--modem-ip <host:port> connect to a Wi-Fi LoRa modem that listens at this` | address (its host set to listen:<port>); can be repeated |
| `--block <ip|net|node> never accept this IP address, network (a.b.c.d/24) or` | node address (32 hex); can be repeated; the dashboard keeps its own list in blocked.txt |
| `--no-relay` | do not relay for hosts behind NAT (only addresses heard over our own radio are published) |
| `--mail-replica-id <address>` | allow this authenticated host in replica selection (repeatable) |
| `--mail-quota-mb <N>` | keep at most N MB of mail for others (default: 200, 0 = no limit) |
| `--min-peers <N>` | keep at least N backbone links, connecting to nodes from the DHT when there are fewer (default 0; maarse-server 6) |
| `--region <name>` | region I forward channel messages for, e.g. dk or nordjylland (can be repeated, at most 8). Without regions everything is forwarded |
| `--strict-region` | without regions: forward only messages without a region |
| `--trunk <port>[:baud] long-distance LoRa trunk: a LoRa node in modem mode with` | a directional antenna; used only when TCP cannot reach the other end, and only for what has to cross |
| `--role <client|repeater|anchor>` | routing role of this host. A client forwards nothing, a repeater forwards, an anchor also splits long routes at the host (12 hops per side). Default: anchor; a phone node: client |
| `--repeater-role` | older form of --role repeater |
| `--no-bordercast` | put every path request from TCP on the radio (default: only for nodes heard over our own radio, or on a retry) |
| `--meshcore-gateway <addr:port>` | accept outbound MeshCore gateways over TLS |
| `--meshcore-worker <addr:port>` | loopback KISS listener for the radio worker (default: 127.0.0.1:5057) |
| `--mqtt <host:port>` | MQTT bridge: publish received telemetry, positions and channel messages as JSON, with Home Assistant discovery |
| `--mqtt-prefix <topic> topic prefix (default: maarse)` |  |
| `--mqtt-user <name>` | user name for the broker |
| `--mqtt-pass <pass>` | password for the broker |
| `--bulletin-key <hex>` | trust signed bulletins from this identity (128 hex digits, printed by the sender's host at start-up; can be repeated). Joins the #bulletin channel, where only verified bulletins are shown |
| `--alert-root <hex>` | accept alert issuer certificates signed by this root key (128 hex digits; can be repeated) |
| `--issuer-key <file>` | issue alerts with this key (kept apart from the node identity; create one with --new-alert-key) |
| `--issuer-cert <file>` | our issuer certificate, sent before our alerts (from --sign-issuer-cert) |
| `--new-alert-key <file>` | create an alert root or issuer key and exit |
| `--sign-issuer-cert <root key> <issuer hex> <name> <days> <out> [events] [max severity]` | sign an issuer certificate with a root key and exit |
| `--radio-quiet` | the radio (USB or Bluetooth) does not beep for new messages |
| `--no-browser` | do not open the browser automatically |
| `--public-map` | share this host's map data (its site, nodes with a shared position, the radio links it hears) with everyone at /api/public/map (for map pages) |
| `--map-url <url>` | where the offline map of Denmark is downloaded from (the address of its map-manifest.json; default: the project's release on GitHub) |
| `--public-traffic` | with --public-map, publish packet counts and recent observations of verified announces |
| `--public-history-hours <n>` | with --public-traffic, keep this many hours of public traffic history so the website can step back (default 24, 0 = none) |
| `--observe-to <peer@key>` | report packet observations over an existing TCP peer link (host:port@128-hex collector identity) |
| `--observe-allow <key> accept observations from this public identity` | (128 hex digits, repeatable) |
| `--share-open-channels` | publish new text and activity from automatically identified open channels (requires --public-map) |
| `--public-channel <name>` | publish new text from this explicitly named channel (public or #name, optionally @region; repeatable, needs --public-map) |
| `--allow-legacy-web-token` | allow deprecated URL query keys during upgrades |
| `--require-key` | ask for the access key from this machine too (for phones and shared computers, where other programs can reach 127.0.0.1) |
| `--service` | run under a service manager (systemd, Task Scheduler): implies --no-browser; a settings restart exits with code 75 and leaves the restart to the supervisor |
| `--help` | show this text |
